values.title: Become the manager you needed in your first year
values.text: I’m Ruth Calloway, a former director of engineering and ICF-certified coach. I help engineers who just became managers run better one-on-ones, give hard feedback and lead without working every weekend.

image.alt: Ruth Calloway talking with an engineering manager at a table by a sunny window

values.title: Managers I have coached lead teams at
Practical help with the parts of managing nobody taught you
values.intro: Coaching is built around your real week: the one-on-one that went sideways, the promotion case due on Friday, the engineer who went quiet in stand-up.

items.title: Better one-on-ones
items.text: A simple structure for weekly one-on-ones that surface problems early, and questions that get quiet engineers talking.

items.title: Feedback you can actually give
items.text: Rehearse the hard conversation with me first, so you walk in with your opening sentences ready.

items.title: Clear priorities
items.text: Decide which engineering work you hand off, and turn down requests that do not need you.

items.title: Fair reviews and promotions
items.text: Write performance reviews and promotion cases that hold up in calibration.

items.title: A confidential sounding board
items.text: Nothing you share reaches your employer, even when they pay. They see attendance and invoices only.

items.title: Help between sessions
items.text: Send a message before a tough meeting and get a reply within one working day.

values.title: I have sat in the chair you are sitting in
values.text: I wrote software for six years before I was handed a team of five and no training. Nine years later I was leading 60 engineers across eight teams. Since 2019 I have coached engineers through the same move, one manager at a time.

items.text: Professional Certified Coach (PCC), International Coaching Federation
Former director of engineering at a Minneapolis healthcare software company
Guest lecturer on technical leadership at the University of Minnesota

image.alt: Ruth Calloway smiling in her office in the North Loop, with bookshelves behind her

steps.title: Free intro call
steps.text: Thirty minutes to talk through your situation and whether coaching with me is the right fit. No pitch and no obligation.

steps.title: Listening tour
steps.text: With your permission, I interview your manager and two or three of your reports, then share what I heard.

steps.title: Sessions every other week
steps.text: Sixty-minute video calls built around what is happening on your team right now, with notes after each one.

steps.title: Closing review
steps.text: We look back at your goals, write down what changed and agree what you keep practicing on your own.

values.title: What changes for the managers I coach
values.intro: From a survey of 164 past clients in January 2026, twelve months or more after their last session.

stats.label: Still managing
stats.text: Chose to stay in management after the hard first two years. Many now lead other managers.

stats.label: Given more scope
stats.text: Were promoted or took on a larger team within 18 months of finishing their program.

stats.label: Fewer regretted exits
stats.text: Average drop in regretted departures on their teams in the year after coaching.

values.title: Start with a free intro call
values.text: Tell me what is going on with your team. If coaching with me is not the right fit, I will point you to something that is.

values.title: Coaching programs for new engineering managers
values.text: Three- and six-month programs for individual managers, a cohort for companies promoting several at once, and single sessions for one decision. Every price is fixed and published.

values.title: Choose the support that fits your first years
values.intro: Every program starts with a free intro call. Most clients’ employers pay from their learning budget, and I invoice the company directly.

plans.name: First 90 days
plans.description: For managers in their first quarter who want a steady hand through the move.
plans.features:
• Six 60-minute sessions, every other week
  • A 90-day onboarding plan in week one
  • Message support between sessions
  • Written notes after every session

plans.name: Foundations
plans.description: For managers in their first two years who want habits that last.
plans.features:
• Twelve 60-minute sessions
  • Listening tour with your manager and reports
  • Midpoint and closing review with your manager
  • Message support between sessions

plans.name: Manager cohort
plans.description: For companies promoting up to six engineers into management at once.
plans.features:
• Six 90-minute group workshops
  • Two private sessions for each manager

  • A summary for the sponsor, with no private details

values.title: Help with one decision or one conversation
values.intro: No program needed. Book a single session when something specific is coming up, or add one to a program at the same price.

items.name: Coaching session
items.description: Sixty minutes on whatever is on your mind this week: a hard conversation, a reorg or a decision you keep putting off.

items.name: Conversation rehearsal
items.description: Practice a feedback or performance conversation with me playing the other person, then try it again.

items.name: Promotion case review
items.description: Written comments on a promotion case or performance review within three working days, plus a 30-minute call.

items.name: 360° feedback report
items.description: I interview up to eight colleagues and write a clear, anonymous summary with three things to work on.

items.name: Manager onboarding plan
items.description: A 90-day plan for a newly promoted manager, built with them and their own manager in two sessions.

items.name: Leadership offsite
items.description: A half-day session for an engineering leadership team, planned with you and followed by a written summary.

values.footnote: Prices in US dollars, excluding sales tax. Companies can pay by card or bank transfer within 30 days.

values.title: The details that make coaching work
values.intro: These commitments apply to every program and every single session.

items.title: Confidential by default
items.text: Employers get attendance and invoices, never notes.

items.title: Flexible hours
items.text: Monday to Friday, 7 a.m. to 6 p.m. Central time, by video or in person.

items.title: Free rescheduling
items.text: Move any session with 24 hours’ notice, or pause a program for leave.

items.title: Notes the same day
items.text: A short summary with the actions you chose, after every session.

items.title: Money-back first session
items.text: If your first paid session is not useful, I refund it in full.

values.title: Not sure which program fits?
values.text: A free 30-minute intro call is the quickest way to find out.

values.title: What managers say a year after coaching
values.text: Stories from engineering managers and the leaders who brought me in, shared with their permission and in their own words.

items.quote: I went from dreading one-on-ones to looking forward to them. Ruth gave me a structure in week one and kept me honest about using it.
items.name: Daniel Reyes

items.quote: The rehearsal sessions were worth the whole program. My first performance conversation went almost exactly the way we practiced it.
items.name: Mei Tanaka

items.quote: Ruth never told me what to do. She asked the question I was avoiding, and then she waited.
items.name: Samuel Okonkwo

items.quote: I stopped reviewing every pull request, and my team started shipping faster. That was the hardest habit to break.
items.name: Laura Bergstrom

items.quote: My director noticed the change before I did. Three months in, she asked who I was working with.
items.name: Jordan Whitfield

items.quote: Having someone outside the company to think out loud with is what got me through our reorg.
items.name: Aisha Rahman

values.quote: We promoted six engineers into management in one quarter. Ruth coached them as a cohort, and a year later all six still lead their teams.
values.result: Regretted departures on their teams down 34% in a year
values.name: Denise Holloway

values.quote: A year ago I was ready to go back to writing code. Today I run two teams, and I am training our next manager the way Ruth trained me.
values.name: Carlos Mendoza

values.title: Want to hear it from a past client?
values.text: After your intro call, I can introduce you to two managers I have coached, so you can ask them anything before you decide.

values.title: Book a free intro call
values.text: Thirty minutes by video to talk about your team and what feels hard right now. I reply within one working day with a few times that suit you.

values.title: Tell me about your team
values.text: Share your role, how long you have been managing and what you would like to change. Calls are by video, Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Central time.
values.messageLabel: What would you like help with?

values.title: Questions before you book
values.text: Something else on your mind? Write to me and I will answer within one working day.

items.question: Can my employer pay for coaching?
items.answer: Yes. Most clients are funded from a learning and development budget. I send your company a short proposal, sign vendor paperwork and invoice them directly.

items.question: Will my manager see what we discuss?
items.answer: No. Sessions are confidential. When an employer pays, they receive invoices and attendance only. If you want your manager involved, we invite them to a three-way review together.

items.question: Do you only coach engineering managers?
items.answer: Mostly. About nine in ten clients lead software, data or infrastructure teams. I also coach product and design managers who work closely with engineering.

items.question: Can we meet in person?
items.answer: Sessions are by video by default. Clients in the Twin Cities can meet at my office in the North Loop at no extra cost.

items.question: What if coaching is not working for me?
items.answer: Tell me. If your first paid session is not useful, I refund it in full, and you can end any program with a month’s notice and a pro-rated refund.

values.title: The first-year manager letter
values.text: One short email every other Tuesday: a question to bring to your next one-on-one and a lesson from my coaching practice, shared without names.
